request.hypothesis: The chair group has insufficient uniform scale. The public size() function multiplies nominal scale by 0.58, consistent with the measured PrimaryItem transform and the visible reduction.
request.observation: The reconstruction chair is substantially smaller: its seat is narrower and its back reaches much lower than in the reference. The green block and room framing appear essentially unchanged.

alternatives.explanation: Camera projection could contribute to the apparent size mismatch, though the matching block and room make a global focal error less plausible.
alternatives.predicted_probe_phenomenon: Scaling only the chair by 1.1 partially improves its apparent size while leaving any camera-related room or block errors unresolved.

alternatives.explanation: Coordinated undersizing of the chair's component geometry could produce a similar silhouette independently of the parent scale.
alternatives.predicted_probe_phenomenon: The entire chair grows and its overall size discrepancy decreases, but any incorrect internal proportions persist.

request.probe_reason: Increase PrimaryItem by 1.1 about its geometry AABB center at fixed camera. This tests whether selective enlargement improves the chair-to-block size relationship while preserving room framing. Both alternatives can also show partial improvement, so this probe cannot uniquely identify the responsible module.

execution.interpretation: Controlled observation, not proof of causal attribution or true 3D accuracy
execution.pivot_rule: Target geometry AABB center; avoids moving geometry center when SceneAct group origin is world zero

probes.interpretation: Controlled sensitivity, not unique causal attribution
